meta.chapterLabel: Lesson 11: Describing Impressions: It Was Beautiful

items.note: Used in どうでしたか (dou deshita ka), "How was it?"
どう (dou) means "how"; でしたか is the past-tense question form of です.
きれい (kirei) is a な-adjective; きれいでした is its plain past form. Compare きれいです (kirei desu), "it is beautiful" (present).

items.hint: used with しゃしんを (photo) as the object
items.note: Combined as しゃしんを とります (shashin wo torimasu), "take a photo."
Asks for a duration or amount; commonly answered with a ぐらい (gurai) phrase, e.g. 5ふんぐらい (gofun gurai), "about 5 minutes."
Dictionary/plain form of the verb; different from あるいて (aruite, "on foot") from Lesson 7, the adverbial form used to say how you traveled, e.g. あるいてうちにかえりました (walked home).

items.scene: after a number, as in 2じかん
items.note: Suffix — attaches after a number to count hours, e.g. ８じかん (hachi jikan), "8 hours."
items.reviewNote: Written 〜じかん in the source | Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 20: Going Places (3): How Do You Go There? (じかん is formally taught as part of the dedicated time-period counters set later, not just incidental vocabulary here)
Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 20: Going Places (3): How Do You Go There? (じかん as an hours counter is formally taught as part of the time-period counter set later)

items.note: Suffix — attaches after an amount of time, money, or people to mean "about" or "approximately." May also be pronounced くらい (kurai).
items.reviewNote: Written 〜ぐらい in the source

items.note: な-adjective meaning hard or tough, as in an arduous experience; たいへんでした (taihen deshita) is its plain past form. Contrast むずかしい (muzukashii), "difficult" in the sense of intellectually hard.
Joins two clauses, translated as "but." Worked example: きのうは いそがしかったですが、きょうは ひまです (Yesterday I was busy, but today I am free).
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 6: Going Places (1): Where Are You Going? (matched on target)

items.note: い-adjective; たのしかったです (tanoshikatta desu) is its plain past form.

items.english: It was fun, it was enjoyable.

items.note: Easily confused with みます (mimasu, "see, watch", Lesson 8) — みせます (misemasu) means "show," not "see."

items.note: い-adjective past: drop the final い and add かったです — おおきい (ōkii) → おおきかったです (ōkikatta desu). Contrast the irregular いい (ii, good), whose past is よかったです, not いかったです.
items.reviewNote: From the GRAMMAR adjective-conjugation chart — regular い-adjective, past affirmative

items.note: い-adjective past negative: drop the final い and add くなかったです — おおきい (ōkii) → おおきくなかったです (ōkikunakatta desu).
items.reviewNote: From the GRAMMAR adjective-conjugation chart — regular い-adjective, past negative
items.target: おおきくなかったです

items.english: It is good, it is nice.
items.note: いい (ii) conjugates irregularly — its negative and past forms are built from よく, not いく.
items.reviewNote: From the GRAMMAR adjective-conjugation chart

items.note: Exceptional inflection — いい (ii, good) does not become いくないです; the negative stem is よく (yoku), not いく.
items.reviewNote: Excluded as a duplicate: chapter-10 already teaches よくないです ("Not good."). The backward de-dup flagged this at build time as already introduced; keeping both made an unanswerable Recognition collision. The earliest occurrence is kept.

items.scene: describing how something you experienced turned out
items.note: Exceptional inflection — the past of いい (ii, good) uses the stem よ (yo), not いい. This same form is also used idiomatically to mean "I'm glad to hear that" — see よかったです later in this deck.

items.note: Exceptional inflection — past negative of いい (ii, good), built from よく (yoku) rather than いく (iku).

items.english: It is beautiful, it is pretty.
items.note: な-adjective, present affirmative; compare きれいでした (kirei deshita), "it was beautiful."

items.target: きれいじゃありません

items.note: な-adjective negative past behaves like a noun + copula: きれい + じゃありませんでした, the same negative-past ending as Lesson 2's じゃありませんでした — no くない form.
items.target: きれいじゃありませんでした

items.note: Same form used in the key sentence きのうは さむかったです (Yesterday, it was cold).
Same form used in the key sentence きのうの おまつりは にぎやかでした (Yesterday's festival was lively).

items.target: きのうはさむかったです

items.note: な-adjective, written かんたん(な) (kantan na) — な appears before a noun but not before です.
な-adjective — see the contrast example きのうは いそがしかったですが、きょうは ひまです (Yesterday I was busy, but today I am free).
Same まつり (matsuri, "festival") already met as (お)まつり in Lesson 7 — お is an optional honorific prefix, both おまつり and まつり are common.

items.note: で (de) here marks Hokkaido as the place where the action happened.
items.target: ほっかいどうでスキーをしました

items.english: I need to be going in a little while.
items.note: Set phrase used when the time has come to leave a place you are visiting.
items.target: そろそろしつれいします

items.note: The past tense of ありがとうございます (arigatou gozaimasu) is used when thanking someone for something that has already ended.
items.target: どうもありがとうございました

items.note: わたし (I) + たち, the plural suffix from Lesson 6 also seen in ひとたち (hitotachi, "people") — together, "we."
て-form of きます (kimasu, "come", Lesson 6) + ください, the same polite-request pattern as まってください (matte kudasai, Lesson 10).
items.reviewNote: Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 19: Making a Request: Please Give Her My Regards (same て-form + ください request construction, not formally taught as a grammar point until later)

Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 19: Making a Request: Please Give Her My Regards (uses て-form + ください (polite imperative request), a construction not formally taught until later — the て-form itself is introduced in ch. 42 and this exact 〜てください pattern is a dedicated grammar point in ch. 43)

items.note: お (o) is an honorific prefix on みやげ (miyage); written (お)みやげ in the source.

items.scene: hearing a positive response after giving a present or offering advice
items.note: Idiomatic use of よかったです (yokatta desu) — literally the past tense of いい (ii, good), "it was good," but used here as a set reaction meaning "I'm glad to hear that."
